summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with a history of polysubstance abuse, atrial fibrillation, coronary artery disease, systolic heart failure, and COPD, was admitted with chest pain and rapid atrial fibrillation after being found unconscious outside in cold weather. He had missed his metoprolol, leading to tachycardia, which resolved with IV diltiazem and oral medication restart. He was diagnosed with frostbite in both feet due to prolonged cold exposure, presenting with discolored, numb, and painful toes. His treatment included pain management with oxycodone and gabapentin, pentoxifylline for circulation, and supportive care with warming, elevation, and wound protection. Lab abnormalities including leukocytosis, elevated lactate, and anion gap metabolic acidosis resolved with supportive care. He remained hemodynamically stable, with no evidence of acute myocardial infarction or infection. He was discharged to extended care with plans for podiatry follow-up, medication continuation, and foot care instructions.
